subject: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@oliveai.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@oliveai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)

Hi Sarah and Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — great to hear more about OliveAI's roadmap for integrating LLM-based summaries into your triage workflow. As discussed, we (Redwood) can run a short POC/trial that demonstrates performance and cost characteristics on a representative slice of your data.

Summary of agreed scope:
- Goal: Validate quality and economics of replacing the current summarization pipeline with a Redwood-served open model.
- Dataset: ~5k tickets (sample to be provided by OliveAI) covering high/medium/low complexity.
- Duration: 4 weeks (engineering + evaluation), target completion end of March.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (suggested acceptance thresholds):
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 300 ms (target 250 ms) for the 1k-token average request profile; cold-start excluded.
2) Throughput: sustained 200 req/s per endpoint under steady-state load (scale plan to hit this with autoscaling).
3) Cost: average inference cost <= $0.0008 per token for the production config (including batching and KV cache benefits).
4) Quality: precision/recall (or human rating) >= 92% on your evaluation set; no more than 2% critical errors (hallucinations that change intent).
5) Availability: no more than 1% error rate in trial window; fallbacks configured for degraded models.

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- OliveAI: provide sample dataset (SLA: 3 business days after agreement), evaluation rubric, and a small label team for human verification.
- Redwood (Lauren / Dev): stand up POC endpoint, provide instrumentation (latency/cost dashboards), and run initial tuning (quantization, batching).
- Joint: weekly check-ins (30m) to review metrics and iterate on prompts/config.

Deliverables during POC:
- POC endpoint URL + API key (Redwood)
- Shared dashboard with p50/p95 latency, tokens consumed, cost breakdown, and quality metrics
- Final POC report with recommendation and next-step options (Dedicated vs Hosted)

Next steps I propose this week:
1) Mutual NDA / SOW (we can reuse the template) — Jordan to share draft by EOD Thu.
2) OliveAI to share sample dataset and evaluation rubric by next Tue.
3) Tech kickoff (30–45m) with Dev and your engineer to agree on input format and auth — propose Wed 2/18.

Attaching: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (POC scope + instrumentation checklist).

If these targets look reasonable, I'll lock the kickoff time and route a short SOW for signature.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@oliveai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@oliveai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)

Thanks Jordan — this is very helpful. A few quick notes from our side after syncing with the product team:
- Latency: can we tighten the p95 target to 250 ms? That's what our UX team is asking for on the baseline use case. If needed we can accept slightly higher cost during the POC so we can test latency-optimized configs.
- Throughput: 200 req/s sounds good for baseline; we'll also need to validate a burst scenario of 600 req/s for up to 60s.
- Quality: we'll provide a rubric and 500 labeled examples to start. Our internal metric is a 4/5 average on subjective summaries (we'll share details).

We can get the sample dataset to you by Tue 2/17. Tech kickoff on Wed 2/18 works for our engineer Tom.

Attaching a short security questionnaire the Security team asked us to start filling out — happy to loop them in if you want to engage early.

Appreciate the clear plan. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Product Lead, AI Platform | OliveAI
sarah.kim@oliveai.com
From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@oliveai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@oliveai.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:58:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)

Looping in a quick note from Security: please include SOC2 type 2 evidence and a short note on data retention/encryption at rest. I've attached SOC2-summary.pdf. Also: for procurement, include an outline of estimated monthly spend for the POC configs (we can use that to pre-approve the card).

- Tom

Senior Engineer | OliveAI
tom.keller@oliveai.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@oliveai.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@oliveai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)

Hi all — happy to support. Two quick items from an ops/offer perspective:
1) If OliveAI wants the tighter latency (p95 <= 250 ms) we recommend a short Dedicated trial (reserved capacity) for the POC window — that gives predictable latency and avoids noisy-neighbor variance. We can spin a small pool for 4 weeks.
2) I've attached a rough POC pricing estimate (poc-pricing-estimate.xlsx) that shows the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for the trial period.

Jordan: I'll coordinate with Finance on a short one-page MSA addendum and a credit card pre-approval workflow so procurement can move quickly.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@oliveai.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@oliveai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Redwood POC for OliveAI)

Thanks everyone — a few technical acceptance criteria and asks from our side so the POC can be run cleanly:
- Provide 5k sample tickets in JSONL with fields: id, text, priority, created_at, expected_summary (if available). An initial 500 labeled examples is fine to start.
- Auth: we'll issue a scoped API key for the POC; please confirm the network/IP ranges if you want to lock down access.
- Logging & telemetry: we'll enable token-level cost logging and p95/p99 latency traces. Please identify any PII in the sample and mark fields to redact.
- Bursts: we'll validate burst to 600 req/s for 60s during a planned test window — please confirm a time for that test during week 3 of the POC.

Proposed immediate next steps for engineering:
1) OliveAI shares sample JSONL and rubric by 2/17.
2) Redwood creates POC endpoint + shared dashboard by 2/20.
3) Joint calibration on quality metrics week of 2/23.

I'll be the technical lead for Redwood — happy to join the kickoff and the calibration sessions.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
